gen-dafont-over-there-gf-cascadia-mono: A fixed-width nib seems to have drawn Over There, vintage and commanding, with Cascadia Mono standing compact below. The plain sans letters, standing like pins, hold up at modest sizes.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-julius-sans-one: Stamped and stern: Over There has a nib-drawn, vintage-military look, while Julius Sans One keeps capitals and lowercase nearly level. One barks orders, the other speaks gently, both with generous spacing.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-lexend-exa: Commanding, nib-drawn Over There heads things up, with Lexend Exa below drawn in one uniform line and a big x-height. Over There earns its keep when it is big and brief.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-lexend-giga: Over There draws vintage-military letters with a fixed-width nib, leaving plenty of white space between neighbors. Lexend Giga is flat, single-weight and widely tracked, so paragraphs of text move along without crowding.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-lexend-mega: Over There looks drawn by one fixed-width nib, vintage and commanding. Lexend Mega, a sans with a body height nearly matching its capitals, gives that stern gesture a friendly partner on the page.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta reads wide and friendly, its curves never thinning and its big x-height leaving little room for ascenders. Over There earns its place when it is big and brief.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera draws a single-weight line like a plotter pen, with open curves and letters spaced like stepping stones. Lexend Tera, a plain sans, lets Over There keep its nib-drawn, military swagger on top.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-lexend-zetta: Over There wears a fixed-width nib look, vintage and commanding, with plenty of white space between its letters. And Lexend Zetta, tall-bodied and widely tracked, takes the quieter job of carrying text.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-montserrat-alte: Over There looks drawn with a fixed-width nib, vintage and commanding, while Montserrat Alternates crowds its lowercase up toward the capitals. Stern meets friendly, and neither blurs the other.
gen-dafont-punkboy-poppins: Poppins runs loose, open curves with no thick-thin flicker. Punkboy does the opposite job, packing bold closed letters hip to hip, while Poppins takes the humbler work of carrying text.
